candidate.answerReason: Every real number greater than 2 is greater than 0, but \(x=1\) satisfies \(x>0\) without satisfying \(x>2\).

methods.label: Check both implications
methods.explanation: \(x>2\) always implies \(x>0\), so it is sufficient. However, \(x>0\) does not imply \(x>2\), so it is not necessary.
methods.levelReason: Uses the definitions of sufficient and necessary conditions with elementary real-number comparisons.
